audit_findings.title: Ongoing strategic-program costs may have been stripped from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: $25 million pretax and $19 million after tax; 8.9% of $281.1 million anchor OE and 8.3% of $300 million FY2025 OE
audit_findings.mechanism: A potentially recurring expense was added back to FY2025 OE, which can raise sustainable OE, the trend anchor and every scenario's operating value.
audit_findings.evidence: While we continue to work on various incremental cost savings programs, operational excellence improvements, and product innovation including sustainable development, if we cannot successfully implement these strategic initiatives, or if the cost of making these changes increases, we may not realize all anticipated benefits, which could materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The $25 million charge and continuing strategic programs are demonstrated, but recurrence of comparable costs is unresolved rather than a proven valuation error. The amount is large relative to anchor OE and is reasonably capable of materially lowering the valuation range if recurring.
audit_findings.action: Trace the FY2025 OE reconciliation, determine which program costs recur after 2025, and rerun the anchor and all scenarios with the unsupported portion of the add-back reversed.

audit_findings.title: Unquantified separation-tax indemnity is a potential senior claim
audit_findings.mechanism: A payment under the Tax Matters Agreement would be a claim ahead of common equity and would reduce the equity bridge or future OE when paid.
audit_findings.evidence: If the distributions are determined to be taxable for U.S. federal income tax purposes, PFL, PEI and Pactiv Evergreen Group Holdings Inc. could incur significant U.S. federal income tax liabilities, and we could also incur significant liabilities.
audit_findings.explanation: The indemnity obligation and triggering conditions are filed facts, but the record supplies no probability, reserve or maximum exposure. A material claim is possible, but neither its occurrence nor materiality can be established from the supplied evidence.
audit_findings.action: Review the Tax Matters Agreement, tax opinion, representations, survival periods, IRS audit status and any triggering post-IPO conduct; quantify probability-weighted exposure and rerun the equity bridge if supportable.

audit_findings.title: Producer-responsibility fees may create a structural cost step-up
audit_findings.mechanism: Recurring EPR fees and compliance costs would reduce OE; conversion capital spending would increase required reinvestment and could also reduce achievable growth or margins.
audit_findings.evidence: These laws require producers to submit reports on packaging and packaging-like product supply, pay fees based on prior-year supply data and comply with state-specific policies to meet recyclability, compostability or reusability criteria.
audit_findings.explanation: Enacted EPR regimes and their requirements are demonstrated, but the supplied record identifies no current expense, forecast amount or implementation impact. This is therefore a forward-looking cost risk rather than a demonstrated omission from present OE.
audit_findings.action: Obtain management's state-by-state 2026–2030 fee, compliance-cost and conversion-capex estimates, net of price recovery, and incorporate them when obligations become measurable.

audit_findings.title: Extreme customer concentration can invalidate steady growth and margin assumptions
audit_findings.magnitude: 48% of revenue, approximately $1,786 million of 2025 revenue computed from $3,721 million total revenue
audit_findings.mechanism: Customer loss, reduced volume, price concessions or higher promotions would reduce OE and invalidate the smooth 0%–5% growth paths.
audit_findings.evidence: Net revenues from our largest customer and its affiliates was 48 % of total net revenues for each of the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023.
audit_findings.explanation: The 48% concentration is demonstrated and is large enough that even a partial deterioration could materially change OE and valuation. No deterioration is demonstrated, but the valuation lacks a customer-specific downside stress despite the exposure being reasonably capable of changing the conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Stress the affiliated customer group's volume, pricing and promotion economics, including partial loss and renewal cases, and rerun OE and valuation under those customer-level outcomes.

audit_findings.title: Historical margins span a supplier relationship that changed from affiliated to independent
audit_findings.mechanism: Changed purchase prices, freight, warehousing, working-capital terms or renewal terms could raise or lower OE and alter the relevance of the historical trend anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: On April 1, 2025, PFL completed the sale of PEI Group, which was a related party through March 31, 2025, to an unrelated party.
audit_findings.explanation: The April 1, 2025 change in counterparty status is demonstrated, but no before-and-after unit economics are supplied. Historical transaction scale was substantial—$360 million of purchases and freight in 2024 and $55 million through March 2025—but those amounts do not quantify the effect of independent pricing. Materiality and direction therefore remain unresolved.
audit_findings.action: Compare pre- and post-April 2025 unit pricing, freight, warehousing, service charges and payment terms, then model each agreement's renewal economics through 2027 and rerun the OE history or forward scenarios as warranted.

audit_findings.title: Unfunded retiree benefits remain a claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $14 million obligation, equal to about $0.07 per diluted share and 0.3%–0.4% of scenario equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: If expected benefit cash payments are not already represented by periodic benefit expense in OE, the obligation should reduce the equity bridge or normalized OE without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: Our postretirement benefit plan is not funded.
audit_findings.explanation: The $14 million unfunded obligation is demonstrated, but even a full separate deduction would reduce value by only about $0.07 per share before the margin of safety, versus scenario values of $16.01–$21.02 per share. That scale cannot reasonably change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Confirm periodic postretirement cost remains in normalized OE; if it does not capture expected payments, deduct the $14 million obligation once in the bridge and verify that no double counting results.
